correctness.rationale: Conditioning yields the exact one-coordinate tied-maximum probability u_n=E[F(X)^(n-1)]. In the no-terminal-atom case, positive tail levels t_j decrease to zero and n_j=ceil(log(1/t_j)/t_j)+1 gives u_{n_j}<=2t_j. Independence across d coordinates gives u_n^d for one candidate index; a union bound gives a_n<=n u_n^d, and t^(d-1) log(1/t)->0 for d>=2. In the terminal-atom case, observing the top vector has probability 1-(1-p^d)^n->1. These arguments cover ties, bounded or unbounded essential supremum, and all d>=2.

value.rationale: The theorem completely classifies a canonical symmetric subfamily of an explicit published open product question for every dimension and every marginal law. It separates the only mechanism capable of sustaining uniform leader probability—a positive atom at the finite top endpoint—from all continuous, mixed without top atom, and unbounded cases. This is structural rather than a routine finite computation.
